source: Dış kaynaklarda saptanan eksik soru tipleri; bağımsız anlatım ve resmî cevap kontrolü (2026-10-12)
answer_convention: İki dilde aynı sırada; ilk şık doğru. Belirsiz cevap aktif bankada yok.
id_convention: Kalıcı idler_010.json; eski veya emekli kimlik yeniden kullanılmaz.

questions.text: Which aeroplane reference field length corresponds to aerodrome reference code number 3?
options: At least 1,200 m but less than 1,800 m
At least 800 m but less than 1,200 m
More than 1,200 m up to and including 1,800 m

questions.text: Which aerodrome ATS units determine the transition level from the QNH reports?
options: Approach Control Office or the Aerodrome Control Tower

questions.text: What makes an aerodrome a controlled aerodrome?
options: An air traffic control service is provided to its aerodrome traffic
It must always lie inside a control zone
It has more than one runway

questions.text: Which temporary AIP change normally requires an AIP Supplement rather than a short ordinary notice?
options: A change lasting three months or longer, or a shorter change needing extensive text/graphics
Only a change lasting more than one year

questions.text: On the normal PAPI approach slope, what does the pilot see?
options: Two red and two white units
One red and three white units

questions.text: What is the normal IFR vertical separation minimum in controlled airspace below FL290?
For Chicago Convention sovereignty, what does a State’s territory include?
options: Its land areas and adjacent territorial waters
Every FIR it provides services in

questions.text: Which rules govern flights over the high seas under SERA?
options: ICAO Annex 2 Rules of the Air without exception
Only the nearest State’s domestic rules

questions.text: You overtake another aeroplane from behind while climbing. Does the climb remove your obligation to give way?
options: No; pass to its right and remain clear until entirely past and clear
Yes, because the climb creates priority
Only if the other aeroplane is also climbing

questions.text: Flashing anti-collision lights in cloud interfere with the pilot’s safe performance of duties. May the pilot reduce or switch them off?
options: No, even if duties are impaired

questions.text: Which ICAO body considers and recommends technical Annex amendments to the Council?
options: The aircraft State of registry alone

questions.text: What does emergency phase mean in ATS terminology?
options: A generic term for uncertainty, alert or distress phase, as applicable

questions.text: A normal VFR flight operates in Class E outside any radio mandatory zone. Which statement is correct?
options: No ATC clearance or continuous two-way radio is required by the class alone, and ATC separation is not provided to VFR
ATC separates it from every IFR flight
An ATC clearance is always required
Two-way radio is always mandatory for all VFR

questions.text: How may a pilot legally fly in a published restricted area?
options: In accordance with the published restrictions or with the relevant State’s permission
Only by filing an IFR flight plan
Whenever the aircraft is below cloud

questions.text: For VFR in Class G above the higher of 3,000 ft AMSL or 1,000 ft above terrain, but below 10,000 ft AMSL, what vertical cloud clearance is normally required?
At an uncontrolled aerodrome, what is the normal circuit-turn direction if no different pattern is indicated?
For VFR in Class G above the higher of 3,000 ft AMSL or 1,000 ft above terrain, but below 10,000 ft AMSL, what is the normal horizontal cloud clearance?
options: Clear of cloud with no fixed distance

questions.text: Under ordinary SERA special VFR rules for an aeroplane by day, what minimum flight visibility must the pilot maintain?
options: 1,500 m, clear of cloud with the surface in sight

questions.text: When passing through the transition layer, when do the usual altitude/flight-level references change?
options: To flight levels at transition altitude in climb; to altitudes at transition level in descent
At transition altitude in both directions
At transition level in both directions
To altitudes in climb and flight levels in descent

questions.text: A powered aeroplane and a sailplane converge at approximately the same level. Which must give way?
options: Whichever is on the left, with no category exception

questions.text: Two aeroplanes converge in VMC at the same level. Only one holds an ATC clearance. Does that clearance itself give right-of-way?
options: No; apply the normal right-of-way rules
Yes, if the aircraft is larger

questions.text: A lower aeroplane has landing priority over a higher one. What may it still not do?
options: Cut in front of or overtake an aircraft already in final approach

questions.text: An airborne civil aircraft must comply with the general rules and which flight rules?
options: VFR whenever visibility is good, regardless of the flight plan

questions.text: What does an ATC clearance authorise?
options: Proceeding under the specified traffic conditions, while other applicable rules still apply
Guaranteed separation from every aircraft in all classes

questions.text: An emergency requires immediate deviation from the current ATC clearance. What follows as soon as practicable?
options: Notify the appropriate ATC unit of the action and seek any necessary amended clearance
Keep the deviation secret if it improves safety

questions.text: On being intercepted, what should a civil aircraft do unless the appropriate ATS unit instructs otherwise regarding the transponder?
options: Follow the interception signals, attempt contact on 121.5 MHz, and select 7700
Turn off the transponder and all lights

questions.text: An intercepting aircraft breaks away with an abrupt climbing turn of 90° or more without crossing your flight path. What does this signal mean?
Two aeroplanes of the same category converge at approximately the same level. Which one must give way?
options: The aeroplane that has the other on its right
The aeroplane that has the other on its left

questions.text: Under SERA, what is the ordinary minimum height for day VFR outside congested areas, without a special permission or take-off/landing exception?
options: 500 ft above ground/water and 500 ft above obstacles within 150 m
1,000 ft above obstacles within 600 m everywhere
There is no minimum outside controlled airspace

questions.text: Before entering a Class D control zone under a special VFR clearance, your radio fails. What is the appropriate action?
options: Remain outside the control zone and arrange a safe alternative
Enter because the original clearance overrides the radio requirement
Enter and rely only on light signals

questions.text: An ICAO certificate carries an endorsement that it does not fully meet an international standard. What is needed for international navigation into another State?
options: Permission from each State whose territory is entered
No permission if a flight plan is filed

questions.text: Under Part-MED, what medical certificate normally permits exercise of PPL(A) privileges?
options: At least Class 2; a valid Class 1 also meets this requirement

questions.text: For SEP/TMG revalidation by experience, without an instructor-training exemption, which package must be completed in the 12 months preceding rating expiry?
options: 12 flight hours, including 6 PIC hours, 12 take-offs/landings and at least 1 hour refresher training with FI/CRI

questions.text: A pilot chooses proficiency-check revalidation of an SEP class rating. What is the normal window immediately before expiry?
Which convention established the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO)?
options: The Convention on International Civil Aviation signed at Chicago

questions.text: What is a prohibited area?
options: Defined airspace over a State’s land or territorial waters in which aircraft flight is prohibited
An area requiring only a flight plan
An area reserved exclusively for VFR

questions.text: A State reserves paid transport between two points in its own territory to its domestic operators. Which right does this illustrate?
options: The first freedom of the air
The second freedom of the air

questions.text: Under Part-FCL, can a CPL holder act as co-pilot in commercial air transport when the appropriate type rating and all other required qualifications are held?
options: Yes, subject to the applicable conditions
No; an ATPL is always required even for a co-pilot
Only if no passengers are carried

questions.text: Under Part-FCL, may a CPL holder act as PIC of a single-pilot aeroplane in commercial air transport if all relevant ratings and other conditions are met?
options: Yes, subject to the applicable CPL and recent-experience restrictions
No; every commercial flight requires an ATPL

questions.text: Which cloud base defines the ceiling when several cloud layers are present?
options: The lowest qualifying cloud layer below 20,000 ft that covers more than half the sky, measured above ground or water
The highest cloud layer, measured above mean sea level
Any scattered layer regardless of coverage
The aircraft’s height above the highest cloud

questions.text: Under SERA, which code normally applies when an aircraft is not receiving air traffic services and the competent authority has prescribed no other code?
Under ordinary SERA rules, may a VFR aeroplane enter Class C airspace without an ATC clearance?
options: No; Class C requires an ATC clearance for VFR as well as IFR
Yes; only IFR flights need clearance in Class C
Yes, if the pilot uses the emergency transponder code
Yes; making a radio call always replaces a clearance
